dspark-draft-1.answer: A stock review should record lead time because it shows how long it takes for an order to arrive after it is placed, which determines how far ahead inventory must be planned. It should also record a reorder threshold so the team knows the exact stock level at which a new order is triggered, rather than relying on memory or guesswork. Together, lead time and reorder threshold help prevent shortages, reduce excess inventory, and keep purchasing decisions aligned with demand and supplier timing.

Receiving ledger, shift 1. The morning crew counted the sealed cartons twice and moved them to the blue rack beside the loading door.
The packing list calls the small brass fitting a sleeve. On the shelf label it is called a collar. Both names refer to the same part.
Leave the open carton on the inspection bench until the second delivery arrives. Record the two delivery numbers on separate lines before releasing the stock.
